title: Jurisprudence and political philosophy
audience: a pre-law college student (any major) preparing for law school and the LSAT
purpose: Compare natural law, legal positivism, legal realism, law and economics and critical approaches; theories of rights and justice; and methods of interpretation such as textualism, purposivism, originalism and living constitutionalism.

weeks.3: Hart and the rule of recognition

blocks.deliverable: Compare the two views on an unjust statute.
Explain how each would decide a case with no clear rule.
Analyze one decision from both perspectives.
Week 7 midterm; summarize three critiques fairly with the replies to them.
Compare two theories of justice on a distribution question.
Apply textualism and purposivism to the same statutory provision.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Jurisprudence essay: take a supplied hypothetical hard case, explain how a positivist, a natural lawyer, a realist and a textualist or originalist would approach it, and defend your own view in 2,000 words.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
